column1: # *** A CANDIDATE SENT FROM ARGENTINA, ANSWERED AND SET ASIDE. ***
# Read 16 September 2026, from two images filed in "Roberto Paul Lerena Documents".
# *** PROVENANCE, CORRECTED BY DAVID ON 16 SEPTEMBER 2026. ***
# This archive first wrote that "somebody pulled it deliberately", inferring an intention nobody had
# stated. That was wrong. *** It arrived unsolicited, in the mail, from a researcher in Argentina, ***
# and David's own view is that it is *** likely no relation. ***
# It is kept, and set out in full for and against, for three reasons: a candidate that arrives from
# a stranger still has to be answered rather than dropped; the age evidence it rests on is real and
# belongs on the record whatever the verdict; and *** the name has already leaked into the family
# tree, where he is entered as "Roberto Paul (Llorens) Lerena" *** - so the reading is in circulation
# and is better refuted in public than left to drift.

column1: # ---- THE CASE FOR, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING ----

column2: *** THE TWO SOUTH AFRICAN DEATH RECORDS BOTH MAKE HIM MID-SEVENTIES. *** The death NOTICE says "77 years - approx". The death CERTIFICATE says "76 years". A birth of 16 August 1872 makes him 77 at his death on 19 March 1950.
column3: *** The Argentine passport's 22 February 1882 makes him 68. The gap is nine years and it is not a rounding. ***

column2: *** THE NAMES. *** ROBERTO - he died as Robert Paul. JUAN - his second son was Ricardo JUAN Carlos, and the enrolment card names his father Juan Carlos. ROQUE - his eldest son was ROQUE Luis Armando.
column3: Three given names, three echoes. Argentine naming is repetitive and this proves nothing on its own, but it is almost certainly why the researcher in Buenos Aires picked this entry out and posted it.

column2: The death certificate registers him as *** LERINA *** and gives his birthplace only as *** "SOUTH AMERICA" *** - not Argentina, not Rosario. The death notice says only "Argentine".
column3: *** Neither South African document was completed by family. *** The notice was signed by Rose Lilian Theys, no relation; the certificate by W. Fraser, whose qualification is "causing burial" - an undertaker. Nobody who knew him supplied any of it.

column2: LLORENS and LERENA are not far apart in a Spanish-speaking mouth written down by an English-speaking clerk, and this family's surname is already documented as Lerena, Llerena, Lorena, Larena and Lerina.
column3: Weak. Llorens is Catalan and ends in -s; Lerena does not. Recorded as the weakest of the four.

column1: # ---- THE CASE AGAINST, AND IT IS HEAVIER ----

column2: *** HIS OWN PASSPORT, WHICH HE SIGNED. *** Argentine passport Serie A no. 07962, Cape Town consulate, 24 December 1940: born ROSARIO DE SANTA FE, 22 February 1882. He signed it "P. A. Lerena" and put his right thumbprint on it.
column3: *** This is the only document in the whole question filled in by the man himself. ***

column2: *** THE 1908 ENROLMENT CARD. *** Clase de 1882. Nacido en Rosario de Santa Fe. Hijo de Juan Carlos Lerena y de Maria Lerena.
column3: Filed in his own name, in Argentina, in his twenties - and it agrees with the passport thirty-two years later.

column2: *** THE PARENTS DO NOT MATCH AT ALL. *** Roberto Llorens and Francisca Fernandez, both Spanish-born, against Juan Carlos Lerena and Maria Lerena.
column3: Not a variant spelling. Different names, different people.

column2: *** THE PLACE DOES NOT MATCH. *** Buenos Aires against Rosario de Santa Fe, three hundred kilometres apart, and the passport names Rosario in his own hand.
*** NOT THE SAME MAN - AND DAVID, WHO WAS SENT IT, SAYS THE SAME. *** The archive reached that independently from the documents before he said so, which is the only reason the working is kept.
column3: Two documents he completed himself say 1882 and Rosario. Two documents completed by strangers after his death say mid-seventies. *** The simplest reading is that a landlady and an undertaker guessed his age high, which is exactly what strangers do. *** The alternative - that he shaved nine years off himself in Argentina and kept the lie for thirty-two years, including on a consular passport where he produced no birth certificate - is not impossible and is why this file is kept open rather than closed.

column2: *** The Llorens family is traceable and this archive has not spent an hour on it. *** Look for Roberto Juan Roque Llorens after 1872 in Buenos Aires: a marriage, a military enrolment, a death. If he lived and died in Argentina, the question closes in an afternoon. *** That is the cheapest open question in this archive. ***
